subject: Error: In sizeAssignAfterRecursing: 'double' is not available or its output type is unknown.

messages.author: 4a248770402c04bc
messages.subject: Error: In sizeAssignAfterRecursing: 'double' is not available or its output type is unknown.
parts:
I'm having trouble compiling a function and getting the error message in the subject line. Here is the full error message:

Error: In sizeAssignAfterRecursing: 'double' is not available or its output type is unknown.
 This occurred for: results <- double(nDim=1)
 This was part of the call:  {
    if(ARG1_n_ < 0) {
      nimStop("invalid argument x < 0")
    }
  results <- double(nDim=1)
  prob <- ddiscnorm(x=ARG4_min_:ARG5_max_,mean=ARG2_mean_,sd=ARG3_sd_,min=ARG4_min_,max=ARG5_max_,log=FALSE)
    for(i in 1:ARG1_n_) {
      multnom_sample <- nimArr_rmulti(size=1,prob=prob)
      results[i] <- (ARG4_min_:ARG5_max_)[which(multnom_sample == 1)]
    }
  return(results)
}

The first function below, ddiscnorm, works fine and is included for the sake of reproducibility (it's used by the second function). The second function, rdiscnorm, is the one causing the error. The un-compiled rdiscnorm function works as expected, but I imagine that's because R plays so loosely with types. From the error message it seems likely that the problem is with the type of my results variable, but I can't think why that shouldn't be a double(1). Is there a way to inspect the type returned by the expression: (min:max)[which(multnom_sample == 1)], which I'm trying to assign to results? Should the problem be clear just from looking at the code?

library(nimble)

ddiscnorm <- nimbleFunction (
  run = function(x = double(1),
                 mean = double(0, default = 0),
                 sd = double(0, default = 1),
                 min = double(0),
                 max = double(0),
                 log = logical(0, default = FALSE)) {

    returnType(double(1))
    # p <- double(1)
    normconst <- sum(dnorm(min:max, mean = mean, sd = sd))
    p <- dnorm(x, mean = mean, sd = sd) / normconst
    for (i in seq_along(x)) {
      if (x[i] < min) p[i] <- 0
      if (x[i] > max) p[i] <- 0
      if (!(x[i] - as.integer(x[i]) == 0)) p[i] <- 0
    }
    if (log) { return(log(p)) } else return(p)
})
ddiscnormC <- compileNimble(ddiscnorm)

rdiscnorm <- nimbleFunction (
  run = function (n = double(0, default = 1),
                  mean = double(0, default = 0),
                  sd = double(0, default = 1),
                  min = double(0),
                  max = double(0)) {

    if (n < 0) nimStop("invalid argument x < 0")

    returnType(double(1))
    results <- double(1)
    prob <- ddiscnorm(min:max, mean, sd, min, max)
    for (i in 1:n) {
      multnom_sample <- rmulti(size = 1, prob = prob)
      results[i] <- (min:max)[which(multnom_sample == 1)]
    }
    return(results)
})
rdiscnormC <- compileNimble(rdiscnorm, showCompilerOutput = TRUE)

Thanks in advance,
Gregory

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Error: In sizeAssignAfterRecursing: 'double' is not available or its output type is unknown.
parts:
Hi Gregory,

The return type from a user-defined distribution (ddiscnorm), if used in a model, should be double(0), i.e. scalar.  But I don't think that's the error you're seeing.

"double(1)" is a type declaration but not a function.  Please try

results <- numeric(length = 1)

I also noticed that you might find rcat (instead of rmulti) to give an alternative way to get what you want.

Perry

messages.subject: FIXED Re: Error: In sizeAssignAfterRecursing: 'double' is not available or its output type is unknown.
parts:
Hi Perry,

Thanks again for your help. I've re-defined my density function to return a scalar, as you advised, since I will be using it in a model.
Following your advice, my random sampling function for the distribution now compiles and appears to work as expected. Thanks for pointing out the existance of rcat as a more elegant alternative to rmulti for this application.

My function now looks like this:

rdiscnorm <- nimbleFunction (
  run = function (n = double(0, default = 1),
                  mean = double(0, default = 0),
                  sd = double(0, default = 1),
                  min = double(0),
                  max = double(0)) {

    if (n < 0) nimStop("invalid argument x < 0")

returnType(double(0))
    prob <- numeric(length = length(min:max))
    for (i in seq_along((min:max))) {
      prob[i] <- ddiscnorm((min:max)[i], mean, sd, min, max)
    }
    return((min:max)[rcat(prob = prob)])

Now on to the p and q functions. I'll post another question if I run into more trouble.

Cheers,
Gregory
